description: ALREADY PORTED, only needed wiring. src/thermo/pr1978.rs was a complete standalone PR78 implementation (kappa, alpha, a_i, a_mix, z_factor, ln_phi, dadt, enthalpy/entropy departure) with PR78_OMEGA_THRESHOLD = 0.491 — it just was not reachable through PropertyPackageModel. The crate CLAUDE.md already listed PR78 among the ported advanced EOS; checking that before writing anything saved duplicating it.

notes.author: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
notes.content:
Done. PR78 reachable as CubicEos::PengRobinson1978 and PropertyPackageModel::PengRobinson1978.

Wired as a CubicEos VARIANT rather than a parallel dispatch path, because PR78 differs from base PR in exactly one thing — the alpha-slope kappa(w). Same Omega_a (0.45724), same Omega_b (0.07780), same (u,w) = (2,-1). So four of the five match arms just gained  and only alpha_slope branches, delegating to pr1978::pr78_kappa so there is ONE definition of the correlation rather than two that can drift.

The enum-dispatch rule paid for itself: adding the variant produced a non-exhaustive-match error at columns/thermo_bridge.rs:508, a second dispatch site I would not otherwise have found.

3 tests: the variant is bitwise identical to pr78_kappa across w = -0.1..2.0; bitwise identical to base PR below the 0.491 threshold and genuinely different above it; shares base PR's prefactors. Measured at w = 1.16 (the heaviest cut a 38 degAPI crude generates): PR kappa 1.80046, PR78 kappa 1.90704, difference 1.066e-1.

HONEST OUTCOME ON THE MOTIVATING CASE: PR78 does NOT rescue the crude column, and I had expected it to. Measured on the same case, all with 'non-finite value in input or K-values':

  PengRobinson      BubblePointFailed at stage 0
  Srk               BubblePointFailed at stage 1
  PengRobinson1978  BubblePointFailed at stage 4   <- furthest, still fails
  Ideal             converges, 38 iterations, 6.7e-7

PR78 gets materially further, which is consistent with the kappa fix helping, but is not sufficient. Crucially the EOS is NOT the culprit: ln_phi was checked directly and returns finite liquid AND vapour fugacity coefficients for this slate at every temperature 400-600 K, for both PR and PR78. The failure is in the bubble-point solver's temperature iteration with a cubic package — a separate defect, now recorded in op-190j.5.

So the crude column stays on ideal K-values, with that decision and its measurements documented at the call site rather than left as an unexplained choice.

notes.author: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
notes.content:
CORRECTION after pulling 44a2001339. My close note said PR78 'does NOT rescue the crude column' and was 'necessary but not sufficient'. That is superseded.

It was necessary. The other half was two defects in the cubic path (select_root accepting a root at or below the covolume; ln_phi then returning NaN rather than None). With those fixed, PropertyPackageModel::PengRobinson1978 is now the DEFAULT for the crude column and it solves: 34 iterations, final error 8.875e-7, monotonic profile, draw temperatures 424.95 / 494.89 / 511.25 / 529.94 / 586.85 K.

So the wiring done here is load-bearing after all — the crude column runs on it.

My supporting evidence was also mis-scoped, and that is the part worth remembering: I checked ln_phi over 400-600 K, the range the COLUMN operates in, and concluded the EOS was fine. The bubble-point solver searches to about 1950 K, and that is where it broke. Probe the solver's search range, not the model's operating range.

title: dwsim: wire PR78 into PropertyPackageModel

description:
User report on GitHub issue #30: "I'm getting blue and black boxes there" in the PDF reader.

Root cause traced to kopitiam-pdf (the PDF rendering engine op-6ez3 chose), not a kovan bug. crates/kopitiam-pdf/src/mupdf/draw_device.rs's TextDevice::show_glyph falls back to painting a solid filled advance-box (in the current fill colour) whenever it can't decode a glyph's real outline -- documented and tested (non_embedded_font_falls_back_to_filled_box), not accidental corruption. The TODO in that file states: "Type1 (/FontFile) and predefined-encoding simple CFF still land here."

So any PDF with embedded Type1 fonts (common in LaTeX-produced PDFs and older scanned/OCR'd reports) or predefined-encoding simple CFF fonts renders those glyphs as solid rectangles -- black for ordinary text, other colours (e.g. blue) for headers/links whose content stream sets a different fill colour. Matches "blue and black boxes" exactly.

Filed upstream: https://github.com/theodoreOnzGit/kopitiam/issues/31 (not filed with a specific fix -- needs a real Type1 charstring interpreter in kopitiam-pdf, a real chunk of work).

Not something kovan can patch around locally without re-implementing font decoding itself. Possible local stopgap discussed with the maintainer: a "known-affected font, this page may render incorrectly" warning banner in the reader, pending the real upstream fix -- not yet decided/implemented.

No specific reproduction PDF yet -- the user's report didn't include one. Asked them for one on GitHub issue #30 to help narrow the upstream fix.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content:
Resolved upstream. kopitiam-pdf 0.2.6 (published to crates.io) adds a from-spec Type1 charstring interpreter (glyph_type1.rs) plus predefined-Standard-encoding CFF resolution -- see https://github.com/theodoreOnzGit/kopitiam/issues/31 for the full writeup and AID-0055 for why hayro-font wasn't used (internal/no public API contract).

Bumped kovan's Cargo.toml pin from kopitiam-pdf 0.2.5 -> 0.2.6, cargo update -p kopitiam-pdf --precise 0.2.6. Verified: cargo check --all-targets clean (native + aarch64-linux-android), cargo test --release: 204 kovan lib tests passing, no new cargo doc warnings, API doc mirror regenerated. GUI binary rebuilt and smoke-tested under xvfb-run (same known no-GPU sandbox limitation as every other round -- can't visually confirm the glyph fix renders correctly in this environment, only that everything builds/links against the new version).

title: kovan-gui: PDF reader shows solid colour boxes instead of letterforms for Type1/predefined-CFF fonts
